utterances.text: Mr. Re, I think the letter is clear enough on what happened. Approximately -- we've heard a comment of Mr. Emmerson that -- at least a note, whether it contains the full name -- the Chamber would like to focus on why the present situation would prevent the start of the testimony of Witness 8, because that's, apart from some -- perhaps some comments and remarks, surprises, let's not focus on -- let's focus on the core issue, and that is why the present situation would -- would necessarily mean that we would not start the testimony of Witness 8 and lose another hour or one hour and a half in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, it's primarily on the basis that the information we got this afternoon would -- if it comes through may present the most relevant and cogent evidence of a person's first statement on a matter relevant to the indictment if it were made in 1999 referable to events in 1998. The other statements - and the Trial Chamber has it now - are from 2001, 2004, 2005, I think, and 2006 and then again yesterday. It is clear from the notes and the statements that the witness's condition mentally may be declining over the years, and our assessment is that the first statement he gave may well be the most accurate one, the most reliable one, and one from which he may be able to refresh his memory, if necessary, but we can't make that assessment without seeing it. And we just, unfortunately, can't get it this afternoon because the person who has it was not in a position to give it to us this afternoon, was in a meeting and wasn't able to do it. That's the problem. Now, in terms of lost court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me ask one question. Are these statements given for purposes of, I would say, investigation in terms of criminal procedure or -- because it looks very much -- of course, we have seen the -- through Witness Andjelkovic the kind of reporting to the Humanitarian Law Centre, which, of course, is not that much focusing on what an investigator would focus on if he was preparing for a file for a criminal case.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The understanding we have, and it's only an understanding, is that based on the employment of the person referred to in the letter, it relates to refugee-type matters and situation. That's a further inquiry we have to make. This was done fairly quickly this afternoon, and we wanted to get the information before the Trial Chamber, and it hasn't been done, I acknowledge, in ideal circumstances. In terms of lost -- lost time in court, our view is that in the circumstances we may lose an hour, maybe an hour and a half, in court if it were to be adjourned this afternoon because Witness 21 is not available. However, I understand that the Defence's view in relation to cross-examining Witness 21, but Witness 21 can certainly give his evidence-in-chief, and we were certainly intending to call him tomorrow to give his evidence-in-chief, and we weren't anticipating he would be cross-examined until after the Easter break anyway. So in that sense, nothing really changes and we certainly wouldn't oppose for the Defence asking for an adjournment tomorrow if we reach the end of it and they felt they needed time to -- to prepare for cross-examining that witness. So, in that sense, very little court time would be lost in the scheme of things if you were to allow us to receive the statement tomorrow and then make the assessment and call Witness 21 instead of Witness 8, just reverse the order, and we would then intend to call Witness 8 after the Easter. Because Witness 21 would probably have to come back after the Easter break anyway the way we're going, because we have videolink on, I think, the 20 -- on the Tuesday after the Easter. So, procedurally, our submission is it doesn't prejudice the Defence and it can be handled -- we may lose an hour to an hour and a half of court time. But ultimately, in our view or our submission, it would -- may assist the Trial Chamber in getting to the truth because of the things you will note in the witness's statement about differing versions in relation to matters more peripheral to the core allegations but may impact upon the reliability of the witness's evidence. If you have the freshest and most contemporaneous statement, and maybe it could be tendered into evidence, we don't know yet, in our submission it would certainly assist the Trial Chamber in getting to the truth of the matter and it's another statement for the Defence to have in their armoury, too, in terms of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, there's some speculation in it not having seen the statement and of course these are two different approaches. One saying another inconsistent statement to say it unfrankly; and the other one, this is the statement which will finally bring us to the truth because it's the first one. Let me just confer with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, the request is denied. The Chamber expects you to start the examination-in-chief of Witness 8. Of course, there's another matter, then the protective measures, of course, first have to be dealt with. But to start with that today, and you're invited as soon as the Telefax copy of the statement arrives to disclose it as quickly as possible to the Defence team. Then I think we are at a point where we could ask the -- Madam Usher to escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, whilst that's being done, I'm going to move on to some questions which require simultaneously to look at a map and some documents, and since that's not feasible on the e-court system, what I propose to do is to give the e-court references to the documents, but to give Your Honours and the witness the documents in hard copy so that the map can be on the screen. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you require the witness to make any markings on the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It might be helpful. It might be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't see an usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These -- she left the courtroom in order to escort the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Will you be using one of the maps already in evidence or new maps?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what I'm going to use is through the e-court system, the large-scale map in the book of maps, which is at map 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But at the moment we haven't used that full-scale map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, we'll continue. Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Antic -- MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'm not objecting. I just want to -- there's one matter concerning the document headed -- well, with a number 0118465.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: That document should be dealt with in private session --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. MR. DI FAZIO: -- and under seal. And I'd like it, if it's to be tendered, the Prosecution says that it should be under seal and could we have --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much -- MR. DI FAZIO: -- private closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's very helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just before I ask you some more general questions about military engagements, at around the time that you were shot and that your father disappeared, can I ask you just for one matter of detail about the incident in which you were shot. And I'm looking at the moment at a statement that records an interview with Slobodan Vukovic, who I think was in the car with you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I just want to read to you a short extract and see if it's an accurate reflection of what happened. It says: "This occurred near Ljubenic on the road from Decane to Pec, about 4 kilometres from Pec ..." That's the right location, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "Slobodan saw a man on the road in uniform, who was armed with an automatic rifle. Slobodan did not specify what kind of uniform the soldier was wearing, but he," that is the soldier, "motioned them," that is the vehicle you were in, "to stop. With Slobodan Vukovic in the car were Cedomir Pavlovic ...?" Does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that the name of the other police reservist, Cedomir Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know either the first or the last name. He started working less than a fortnight before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So do I take it from that, you're not sure whether that is his name or not?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Also in the car then was Momo Antic, which is I think you, and Dimitrije Radovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, may I ask you one clarification. You say that you're quoting -- you're looking at the statement that records an interview with Slobodan Vukovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then we get in quotation marks on the screen: "Slobodan saw a man on the road in uniform ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which is -- is the report such that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's in the third person --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the one that drafted it --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Exactly so, exactly so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understand. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again quoting: "Slobodan was from Rausic in the municipality of Pec. Cedomir was from Bijelo Polje in Pec and Momo was from Decane." And then this: "Slobodan told me that they hit something with their van, but he was unsure if they had hit the man motioning them to stop or just his rifle. The men continued on their way and they were opened fire upon. Slobodan says that seven men fired upon the vehicle" -- I'm sorry, "upon the van which was pierced in many places." Now, I just want to be clear. You told us, I think, at one point that the vehicle did hit one of the men. The account that I've just read to you suggests that the man who was hit was motioning the vehicle to stop, was either hit or his rifle was hit, the vehicle carried on, and it was after that, that fire was opened upon the vehicle. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slobodan hit him with the rear part of the vehicle, and that man had come out of the canal. He didn't hit his rifle, he hit him. He couldn't open fire after that. If anyone had opened fire, there was somebody who was with him in the canal. There was several of them, or rather, more than just seven, and I saw them with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's helpful, but I just want to clarify one part of that answer. Is it the case then that Slobodan hit this man with the vehicle before the shots were fired?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes -- no. First there was fire when we came around the bend. We left the first ambush, and right after that there was a soldier in uniform with a weapon, and then Slobodan hit that man with the rear part of the vehicle. He was not firing upon us. There may have been someone else who had been there with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you're sure, are you, that shots were fired before he knocked into the man in uniform?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, if you have dealt at least with this small portion, I would like to seek some clarification. Mr. Antic, you said the shots went under the car, they were bad in handling their weapons. Could you tell us when the shooting started before the car hit this person who came out of the canal - would you please - did these first shots already hit the car, or was the car hit by the shots only after the person had been -- the person who came out of the canal had been hit by the car? So let me try to split that up --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As soon as they saw our uniforms, they opened fire. There was no attempt to stop us or anything else. First they opened fire upon the car, but I guess they were a bit frightened. They looked away while they fired. After that, the bullets went under the car. They only managed to pierce only one left tire, but it was good luck for us that it was an all-wheel-drive vehicle and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there for a second. Did the shooting stop after you had hit this man who came out of the canal and who was not firing at the car? Did it, the shooting, stop or did it continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but on that same day, the 25th of May when I was wounded, there was a commander when going to Streoc --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm -- I'll stop you there because I want to have very focused information. When you say "yes," did you mean to say that the shooting stopped or that the shooting continued after the car had hit this person coming out of the canal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We -- when we came upon that man who came out of the canal, the shooting stopped; however, two to three hours later there was firing again from the direction of the Streoc mountain. There were -- there is a pine forest, and they killed a police commander there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that was not at the same place at the same moment. You said so once the car hit this person --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the shooting for that moment for that place stopped. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you earlier said, And the bullets went all under the car.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not all of them. Some hit the car itself, some went under it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the car was hit already by the bullets before this person was hit by the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. It was not a van. It was a Golf passenger car, a small vehicle. It was not a van.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In my question in English the word "van" did not appear, but let me then repeat the question. Was the car in which you were already hit by the bullets before there was this collision where the car hit the man coming out of the canal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And when you were injured, when the bullet struck your leg, was that before or after the man had been knocked down?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After, when we were supposed to leave the place of ambush.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So there was some firing that took place after the man was knocked down, as you were leaving?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was some hundred metres away from the place of the first ambush. The one who came out of the canal, he didn't open fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just see finally if I can clarify this, because I think I understand what you're saying, but see if I've got it right. First of all, you were driving along the road, and you say some shots were fired but luckily they only struck the tire. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Then the man came out and was knocked over. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: After the tire of the vehicle had been struck, did the man then get out of the canal and get knocked over?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, after that. In the first ambush, they managed to hit a tire and we could hear the bullets; but after the place of the first ambush, perhaps a hundred metres away to the right-hand side, he was in the canal. And as soon as he saw the car coming, he jumped on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Right. So that's much clearer. So, first of all, some bullets were fired and all they hit was the tire. Then you drove on and, about a hundred metres later on, an unarmed man in uniform stood in the road and was hit; and after that, they opened fire on the vehicle and that's when you were injured?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was injured at the place of the first ambush. When we came out of the curve, they were standing next to the road going to Decani. As soon as they spotted our uniforms, they opened fire on the vehicle. First they hit Dimitrije Radovic, and then leaving the place of ambush I was hit by a fragmentation bullet. A hundred metres further down the road, there was this soldier who had a weapon in his hand and who jumped out on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And as far as you could see from where you were sitting, was he deliberately run over or was it an accident?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was deliberate. He had a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It was a war situation, I suppose?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you some more questions about what was going on, on the ground, in terms of the broader war situation on the west side of the main Peje to Gjakove road, because Lloqan is on the west side of the main Peje to Gjakove road, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response].

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we have up on the screen, please, Rule 65 ter, Exhibit number 01006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that will be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit D32, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I take it that you would want to tender that, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In a moment, you'll -- do you have a map on your screen in front of you? Not yet?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It usually takes some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if we can please enlarge it to the left-hand side of the map, and I'm afraid what we need to do is to look a little further down, so south of Peje, but further down still. And then pause there, if you would, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's not as clear on the screen as ideal, although we, all of us, I think, have access to a slightly crisper copy, other than you, I'm afraid. Let me see if I can ask for your assistance for a moment. If we focus in on Decane, which is --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just a little bit further north. That's it. Stop there -- stop there, if you would.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Immediately beneath Decane, do we see Lloqan, the village where you lived?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if you could just help us with some other locations for a moment, if you would. Can you see just to -- on the map just to the left of the ring around Decane, a placed called Huljaj, H-u-l-j-a-j, so to identify those locations?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's further off from Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Could you just assist us by putting a circle around it, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it without my glasses. I can't see it without my glasses -- MR. DI FAZIO: For the assistance of Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- this witness experienced some difficulties yesterday, and we had to get him special --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see -- MR. DI FAZIO: -- eye spectacles from VWS --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't want to force the witness to strain his eyes during the course of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you see it there, can you, on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the problem is that he said he couldn't see it because he didn't have his glasses.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I thought a moment ago, he said that he did see it. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Can you see --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Perhaps if we focus in a little --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if we focus in.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you see it there to the left of the ring around Decane, H-u-l-j-a-j? Just south of the Bistrica River.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: The earlier comment of the witness was --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There, there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- that's further off from Decane, just out of his general knowledge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just for our assistance could you --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If we just look south of Lloqan on that same screen, can you see a place called Slup, S-l-u-p? Do you see that, just south of Lloqan? If you look immediately underneath Decane -- Lloqan, can you see a -- the word S-l-u-p, Slup?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could even more move in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It might be this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we just focus in for the witness, if we could, please, on Slup and Voksa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, it can't be focused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The last marking will be lost if we zoom in.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Drenovac, it's right there. What exactly did you say? Slup?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Slup and Voksa.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now we moved. Could you please try to find again Locane, who's now a little bit further up. Do you see Locane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There it is, Voksa and Locane. Locane, right there. Voksa, Slup.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Again, just so we're clear, these are two of the closest villages to where you lived, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then if we just look a little bit further down just to orientate ourselves - I won't ask you to mark it because we can look at the map separately - but if we can just follow it down a little further to Junik, and just to the right of Junik is there -- is there a village there called Sac? Do you know that village, S-a-c? Just to the right of Junik on the road leading towards the main Peje-Pristina road, just outside the red mark, do you see Sac?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: S-a-c --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, do you see that? Do you know that village?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not Sac, I can't remember what it was called.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. And if we could just for a moment move --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never heard of this village.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Near Junik.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sac.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. If we could just move a little bit further south along the same road, please, until we reach Ponosevac. I just want to identify some of the other villages along the way. Just pausing there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we just go up a little bit, keeping Ponosevac at the bottom of the screen. Pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I just want to ask you with one or two of these other villages. You know Molic at the top of the screen there, right at the very top along the yellow road? You know Molic?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard of it, yes. I've never been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you know Brovina?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Heard of, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Stubla?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Heard of.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Ponosevac?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Likewise.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: These are all villages along the road that leads directly to Lloqan, aren't they? They're on the same road. We can follow that yellow road all the way up to Lloqan, can't we?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Locane is quite far from Ponosevac. You must first head for Junik and then for Voksa, and then from Voksa you go to Locane or the other way around. Junik, Lastavica, Trilje [phoen], Crnora -- Donji, Crnobreg.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand. But they're all on the same road. This road, this yellow road marked on the map, takes you all the way to Lloqan; yes? Yes?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just one final location, if I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we can just go up a tiny bit on the map just above Molic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Pausing there, you see the village to the right there, Nivokaz? You know that village as well?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Nivokaz is near Junik. When you go from Junik to Hrastica on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we now move into closed session briefly, please, Your Honour. Or private session, rather.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For the record, the relevant document identification number of the document that was shown in private session - and this would obviously be tendered under seal - is 1D040172. Can I ask that that be marked for identification under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D33, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The next document that I want to take you to, you have, I think, in front of you as well. Could you just look at the other document that's on the desk in front of you, please, Mr. Antic, because for that we have the original Serbian, as well as the English translation, and this is not a document that needs to be under seal or in private session. It is document identification 1D040008, with an English translation linked at 0009.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D34, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Antic, this is an order that was issued the day before your father disappeared, and it was issued by General Pavkovic, who you probably have heard of, have you?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think Pavkovic betrayed him. He didn't know Pavkovic at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You know who General Pavkovic is, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Just so that we're clear, he was in overall command of VJ forces in Kosovo and was commander of the Pristina Corps 3rd Army. Is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is an order that he issued on the 28th of May, very urgent, personally to the commander: "Decision on engagement?" And it reads as follows: "The 3rd BVP, Military Police Battalion, with its main forces, is to increase the security on state borders and secure the zone. Its auxiliary forces together with a tank platoon are to carry out an attack in the following direction: The GPMI border post." And then this: "The village of Huljaj," that's the village that we looked at earlier on, isn't it, which is just to the west of Decane.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response].

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The village of Locane, that's your village, isn't it, together with a tank platoon. And then it says: "On stand-by at 4.00 in the morning, 0400, on the 29th of May." Did you realise that the night your father disappeared the VJ forces were launching an attack in Lloqan?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in Locane.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that's the order that we have, Mr. Antic. Let's continue --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Locane.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You can see it on the document in front of you, I think, can you? Or is it not possible for you to read? You see Locane there? It's in the second paragraph, first line in the Serbian. Do you see? Huljaj and Locane?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then it continues: "With part of the forces, block the roads in the following direction: Decane to the village of Locane, Slup Voksa towards Junik, from the right side, from the Varic area?" So the order, at least, that was being issued was for the road from Decane to Lloqan to the blocked, and the roads to Slup and Voksa to be blocked on that night. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then just picking it up a little further down, a task is recorded for the 2nd Battalion of the 52nd Mixed Artillery Brigade in the area of Decane? "For the purpose of supporting the MUP forces and the VJ units in breaking and destroying the Siptar rebel forces, planned fire is to be opened in the following areas: Skoze, Molic, Hordup, Molic stream, Bljinista, Brovina, Nivokaz, and Stuble. Those are all the villages, I think, we looked at a few moment ago on the map.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then it was to be extended to Sac in the area of Junik, which was the little village I think you said you didn't recognise the name of. Were you aware that there was a major military assault taking place by the Serbian forces, by the Yugoslav Army, all the way along that road, including your own village, on the night that your father disappeared?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true. I never heard of it, and it's just not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of course by then you were in hospital in Belgrade, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which month?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The 28th of May, 1998. By then you were in hospital in Belgrade, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And do you know anybody who you have spoken to who was in that area on the 28th of May, that night, the 28th to the 29th that you've personally spoken to?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Emmerson. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No questions. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: No re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Hoepfel has a question for you, Mr. Antic. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, just to clarify the hour of this ambush you described when there was the shooting on the road. Was it in the morning or in the evening?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wounded. Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the morning, five minutes to 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one question for you as well, Mr. Antic. You earlier spoke about Ramush Haradinaj's army, and then you were invited to explain what you meant by that, and then you said that is the KLA. Is there any -- do you have any personal knowledge that links the KLA to Mr. Ramush Haradinaj? So I'm not talking about what you may have read in the newspapers or what you may have seen on television. Do you have any personal knowledge, any personal observation, which links Mr. Haradinaj to the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because Ramush's army, his personal army, first wounded me on the 25th of May, 1998. On the 28th, the evening of the 28th, again his army, the KLA, took my father away. Vida Simic was across the way, the headquarters, they sprayed it with bullets. So what do you mean when you say I have no personal knowledge since he was the greatest war criminal, and it's unimaginable the sort of thing that he did. He didn't kill my father with a bullet. If he had killed him with a bullet, God would have had mercy on his soul, perhaps. Maybe it wasn't he who killed him personally. He was the commander. Maybe it was his army that killed my father.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that this brings quite some emotion to you. Thank you for this answer. I take it that the questions of the Bench have not triggered any need for further questions. Mr. Antic, you've answered all the questions of the parties. You've answered the questions of the Bench. You came a long way. I'd like to thank you for coming and for testifying before this Court. This concludes your evidence and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to invite the parties to think about a more efficient way of proceeding, especially the last episode with the maps. I take it that it's fully in line with traditional and classical introduction of evidence, but of course to go through all the villages where the witness has a difficulty to see them and then him to say that I heard about it but I don't know where it is; whereas, we have a clear map in front of us, where the context was perfectly clear, I think, to the Chamber. So perhaps the last question should have been the first one; the question being: Were you aware of any military operations including so-and-so going on at the time. If the witness would say, No, I'm not aware of that, then, of course, you couldn't introduce the documentary evidence through this witness, but it might be material since, I take it, that the authenticity is not challenged by the Prosecution. That could have been presented from the bar table so that -- or even make stipulations on the matter. But now we go through it quite some detail with -- well, you can sometimes already expect approximately what happens. Of course it should be properly put to the witness but whether the way in which it was done was the most efficient way is another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Madam Registrar, we have documents introduced through the witness marked for identification. We have -- if you could just read the numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, with this witness we had document -- Exhibit Number D32, 33, and 34.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Di Fazio? I assume that they're all tendered into evidence. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D -- MR. DI FAZIO: Oh, no, there's no objection apart from the one that should remain under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's one under seal, Madam Registrar, that would -- that is number ...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. D33 is under seal. MR. DI FAZIO: Other than that, no problems at all with their full admission into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. They are admitted into evidence, D33 under seal. Mr. Re, is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness, but the Chamber would like to start the -- this witness in a different way. We still have to deal with the -- with the request for protective measures. The Chamber would like first to hear from the Defence, but the Chamber might want to put some questions to this witness before we decide on the request for protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We could cut matters short. The Chamber has asked for a kind of informal notification of the position of the Defence. If the Defence would be willing to file those e-mail messages under seal, confidentially, then everything is on the record, we know what we're talking about, and we don't have to invite the Defence to repeat what was already briefly set out. If you would like to add anything, then we'll turn into private session and you're invited to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I have nothing to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and we'll file the e-mail under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Nothing to add. We'll file the e-mail under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Excellent suggestion, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Re, you have seen the e-mail messages which will now be filed confidentially. The Chamber would like to ask perhaps one or two or three questions to the witness before deciding the matter. Is there any need from you to add any observation at this moment, or would you rather wait until we have put the questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There is nothing from our perspective, and Mr. Kearney will be dealing with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Kearney, the question is now addressed to you. No need at this moment. Then we have to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has decided that the protective measures are granted as sought; reasons to follow. I further suggest to the parties that I deviate from what I said earlier, that is to ask the witness to make another solemn declaration and just remind him that he, also for this part of the proceedings, is bound by the solemn declaration. I see there seems no objection to that. Witness 8, you earlier gave a solemn declaration. That solemn declaration that you will speak the truth still applies, and you will now first be examined by Mr. Kearney, who's counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Kearney, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, thank you very much. At the outset, I wonder if I could ask the Trial Chamber to ask the witness to take his headphones off for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness 8, could you take off your headphones for a second? Thank you. Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you. Your Honours, as members of the Trial Chamber may have noticed during the initial swearing-in process of this gentleman, he is an older gentleman. He is somewhat unsophisticated. The Prosecution believes his memory is failing. I would invite counsel to make their comments in that regard, but I believe that's the case. And given that, I am going to seek to narrow the scope or the focus of my direct examination to several points that are directly related to the gravamen of the counts, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And I'm going to confine my examination to that based on his state right now. Of course, I would invite -- the Prosecution would not object to the Defence to cross-examine this witness on any subject they feel appropriate. Obviously, the Court -- members of the Trial Chamber have that same opportunity, but I just wanted to alert members of the Trial Chamber that is my intent at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if I might just make this observation. Difficult as this process may prove to be, there are five witnesses in this case who the Prosecution rely upon as giving direct testimony of my client's participation in crimes; three of them have already given evidence, this is the fourth. I cannot confine cross-examination. I know what Mr. Kearney has in mind. The proposal of the Prosecution is not to elicit from this witness any evidence about his alleged visit to the Lake Radoniq canal or to Hotel Pastrik, and I know the reason for it also is because the accounts he has given both in writing and in his proofing sessions are incredible and inconsistent with the facts. However difficult it may be, cross-examination of this witness is going to necessarily take some time and is necessarily going to need to traverse a fair amount of material so that Your Honours are in a position to assess whether he's a reliable witness because he's the only witness in respect of those counts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think Mr. Kearney clearly indicated that his approach would have no consequences for the scope of the cross-examination by the Defence. Mr. Kearney, to -- the Chamber had already considered whether or not we should invite the Prosecution to -- perhaps not to limit its examination-in-chief, but first to focus on what you consider to be the most important elements, since you indicate now that you will do that without being encouraged to do so. There's no need for the Chamber to express any further thoughts about that. Of course, you will also understand that on the basis of the experience of the last 15 minutes in court, that the Chamber will, of course, hear the evidence, but at the same time will give it some consideration to what extent the evidence, we still do not know what is there to come, whether it's such that it could assist the Chamber. We'll closely monitor that but, of course, first of all hear the evidence as -- as it is given. Then I take it that we can invite the witness to put on his earphones again, or not yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is one additional matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think ... Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: We have prepared a document relating to this gentleman's personal details, it's 65 ter 1218. Normally, at this stage, I would ask the Trial Chamber to simply show it to the witness just to have him read it to see if he agrees with it and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's impossible, it seems, at this moment from -- at least from his earlier answers that ... We'll then turn into private session if you read to him what is on the pseudonym sheet, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, I'd like to do that, if I may, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 8, you said you were born in the Gjakove region of Kosovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How long did you live there?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many years we have lived there, but from Cermjan we went to Gjakove, and there we lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, when you finally left Kosovo, were you still living in the village of Gjakove at the time?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, for 16 years or so we lived in Gjakove, but now I cannot tell you how many years have passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And when you say that "we lived in Gjakove," who are you referring to, please?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I refer to myself, to my brother, to the entire family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm going to seek to elicit the name of his brother at this point. Does the Court wish to go into private session briefly or can we proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'd rather keep it on the safe side.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There is one brief matter I need to raise. It doesn't need to detain the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the witness cannot leave at this moment without protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In which case, it is a matter that I ought to deal with in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we will return into private session. Yesterday I'd forgotten to return into open session when we adjourned, and that was a mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I'll not make the same mistake as yesterday; that is, not to return into open session before we adjourn. We stand adjourned until tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 5th day of April, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.06 p.m.,
